basic_information.name: OpenAI File Search / Web Search (Responses API)
basic_information.creator: OpenAI
basic_information.description: OpenAI File Search and Web Search are built-in hosted tools available through the Responses API that provide turnkey RAG capabilities. File Search allows developers to upload documents to a managed Vector Store, where OpenAI automatically parses, chunks, embeds, and indexes them, enabling hybrid semantic + keyword retrieval in a single API call. Web Search enables models to retrieve and ground responses with real-time information from the public web, returning inline citations. Together, they eliminate the need to manage separate embedding pipelines, vector databases, or search infrastructure, making RAG accessible to any developer using the OpenAI API.
basic_information.release_date: March 11, 2025 (Responses API general availability); File Search originally in Assistants API v2 April 2024; Web Search tool added in preview March 2025
basic_information.github_stars: N/A — proprietary hosted service; OpenAI Python SDK has ~25k+ stars but is the client library, not the service itself

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Serverless managed API. File Search uses a hosted vector store backend with automatic document parsing, chunking, and embedding. Web Search uses a proprietary web index with search-augmented generation. Both are invoked as tools within the Responses API, which orchestrates tool calls alongside LLM inference in a single stateless API call.
technical_architecture.language: Python SDK (openai-python), Node.js SDK, REST API. Backend infrastructure is proprietary (likely Go/Python/C++ based on OpenAI's stack).
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: File Search internally uses OpenAI's embedding models. text-embedding-3-large supports up to 3,072 dimensions (can be shortened to 256 or 1,024). text-embedding-3-small supports up to 1,536 dimensions. The specific model used internally by File Search is not publicly documented but is believed to be text-embedding-3-large or a variant.
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: Not publicly documented for File Search internals. Uses both vector similarity search (dense retrieval) and keyword search (likely BM25 or similar). Results are then reranked before being returned. The vector index type (HNSW, IVF, etc.) is not disclosed.
technical_architecture.scalability: Each vector store supports up to 10,000 files. Maximum file size is 512 MB per file. Multiple vector stores can be attached per request. No disclosed horizontal scaling controls — OpenAI manages all infrastructure. For Web Search, scalability is handled entirely by OpenAI's search infrastructure with no user-configurable limits beyond API rate limits.
technical_architecture.deployment_options: Cloud-managed only (OpenAI API). Also available through Azure OpenAI Service for enterprise customers. No self-hosted or on-premise option. Data residency available in US, Europe, UK, Japan, Canada, South Korea, Singapore, Australia, India, and UAE for eligible enterprise customers.

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: File Search: Hybrid retrieval combining dense vector search (semantic similarity) and keyword/sparse search (BM25-style), followed by automatic reranking to select the most relevant chunks. Web Search: Proprietary web index search with two modes — (1) non-reasoning quick lookup where the model sends a query and gets top results, (2) agentic search with reasoning models (o3, o4-mini) where the model iteratively searches, analyzes, and decides whether to continue searching.
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: Automatic chunking with configurable parameters. Default: max_chunk_size_tokens=800, chunk_overlap_tokens=400. Configurable range: max_chunk_size_tokens between 100-4,096 tokens, chunk_overlap_tokens up to half of max_chunk_size. Supports 'auto' and 'static' chunking strategies. No support for semantic chunking, RAPTOR hierarchical chunking, or document-structure-aware chunking — purely token-based splitting.
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: Built-in automatic reranking. File Search runs both keyword and semantic searches, then reranks results to pick the most relevant chunks before generating the final response. The reranking model/algorithm is not disclosed. Users can configure the number of results returned (num_results parameter) but cannot plug in custom rerankers.
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: File Search supports text extraction from various document formats including PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, CSV, HTML, MD, TXT, JSON, and more. However, it operates on extracted text — no native image/chart/table embedding from within documents. The Responses API itself supports text, images, and audio as input modalities, but File Search specifically is text-retrieval only. For images within PDFs, content may be lost during text extraction.
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: None. File Search is purely vector-based retrieval with no knowledge graph construction, entity extraction, or graph-enhanced retrieval capabilities.
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: Strong built-in citation support. File Search returns file_citation annotations with file_id, filename, and the exact quoted text from the source document. Web Search returns URL citations with inline source attribution. Both tools enable the model to ground its responses in retrieved content and provide verifiable source references.
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: Users can control the number of chunks retrieved via num_results parameter to manage token usage. The include parameter allows filtering which parts of the response to return. Configurable chunk sizes help balance retrieval granularity vs. context window consumption. No built-in compression or summarization of retrieved content — raw chunks are passed to the model.

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: File Search: Reported latency ranges from several seconds to 45-60 seconds for 500KB vector stores, depending on query complexity and store size. Typical RAG queries via File Search average ~11.17 seconds compared to ~7.36 seconds for traditional custom RAG pipelines (roughly 3.8 seconds slower). Web Search: Varies by mode — quick lookups are faster (a few seconds), agentic search with reasoning models can take significantly longer as the model performs multiple iterative searches.
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: Not publicly benchmarked. Subject to OpenAI API rate limits which vary by tier (Tier 1 to Tier 5). File ingestion throughput depends on document size and complexity. Vector store creation and file processing are asynchronous operations.
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: No published recall@k, NDCG, or MRR metrics for File Search specifically. OpenAI's embedding models perform well on standard benchmarks: text-embedding-3-large achieves 64.6% average on MTEB and 54.9% on MIRACL (multilingual retrieval). Web Search accuracy has received mixed reviews — some users report stale results (months/years old news), while others find it effective for current information retrieval.
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: No dedicated File Search benchmarks published by OpenAI. A LlamaIndex comparison (2026) found that traditional RAG was faster than agentic file search (7.36s vs 11.17s average). OpenAI published BrowseComp benchmark for web browsing agents but this is for ChatGPT deep research, not the API web search tool directly. text-embedding-3-large MTEB score: 64.6% average (up from 61.0% for ada-002).

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: Direct integration via OpenAI's Python and Node.js SDKs. LangChain supports OpenAI as an LLM provider and has wrappers for embeddings, but File Search as a tool is typically used directly via the Responses API rather than through LangChain's retriever abstractions. LlamaIndex similarly integrates OpenAI models but File Search is a managed tool, not a pluggable retriever. The Responses API's tool-use paradigm means it competes with rather than integrates into external RAG frameworks — you use File Search OR you build your own pipeline with LangChain/LlamaIndex.
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: File Search works with all OpenAI models that support the Responses API: GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4.1-nano, o3, o3-mini, o4-mini, and GPT-5 series. Web Search works with GPT-4o, GPT-4o-mini, GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1-mini, o3, o4-mini. Dedicated search preview models (gpt-4o-search-preview, gpt-4o-mini-search-preview) also exist for Chat Completions API. Not compatible with non-OpenAI models (Anthropic, Google, Mistral, open-source).
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: Yes. The Responses API added support for remote MCP servers in May 2025. Developers can connect to external MCP servers (Stripe, Shopify, Twilio, etc.) alongside File Search and Web Search. OpenAI joined the MCP steering committee. No additional cost for MCP tool calls — only billed for output tokens.
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: File Search: Direct file upload via API (PDF, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, CSV, HTML, MD, TXT, JSON, and other text formats). No native connectors for S3, GCS, Confluence, Notion, Slack, or databases — files must be uploaded programmatically. Web Search: Searches the public web (proprietary index). MCP integration enables connecting to third-party services. Custom GPTs in ChatGPT provide a no-code file upload interface.
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: Limited built-in observability. The Responses API returns usage metadata (input/output tokens, tool call details). No native integration with LangSmith, Arize Phoenix, Langfuse, or OpenTelemetry. Developers must build their own logging/tracing on top of API responses. OpenAI provides a Dashboard with usage analytics and rate limit monitoring.

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: Pay-per-use with multiple components: (1) File Search: $2.50 per 1,000 search queries + $0.10/GB/day vector storage. (2) Web Search: tool calls billed per 1,000 calls (pricing varies by model and tool version, approximately $25-50 per 1,000 calls for standard models, $30 for gpt-4o-search-preview) + search context tokens billed at model's input token rate. (3) Underlying model tokens (input/output) billed at standard model rates. (4) Embedding creation costs if using the Embeddings API separately.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: First 1 GB of vector storage is free. No free tier for search queries or web search calls. Standard OpenAI API free trial credits ($5-18 depending on region) can be used for File Search and Web Search.
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: File Search at scale: 10GB vector store = $1/day storage + $2.50 per 1,000 queries. 100GB vector store = $10/day ($300/month) storage. 1M file search queries/month = $2,500. Web Search: 1M web search calls/month at ~$30/1K calls = ~$30,000/month + search context tokens. For comparison, self-hosted RAG with open-source tools (pgvector + open-source embeddings) can be 10-100x cheaper at scale but requires engineering investment.
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: TCO includes: (1) Vector storage ($0.10/GB/day beyond 1GB free), (2) File search queries ($2.50/1K), (3) Web search calls ($25-50/1K depending on model), (4) Model input/output tokens at standard rates (e.g., GPT-4o: $2.50/1M input, $10/1M output), (5) Search context tokens for web search at input token rates. For gpt-4o-mini web search, a fixed block of 8,000 input tokens is charged per call. No infrastructure management costs. Potential hidden cost: vector store storage can be much larger than raw file sizes due to embeddings and parsed content.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Leader in managed RAG services by virtue of OpenAI's dominant market position in LLM APIs. File Search and Web Search are deeply integrated into the most widely used commercial LLM platform. Competes with Google Vertex AI RAG Engine, Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases, Cohere RAG (Command R), and Perplexity Sonar API. Key differentiator is seamless integration with OpenAI's model ecosystem and zero-infrastructure RAG setup.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Navan (AI-powered travel agent using File Search with dedicated vector stores per user group), Box (enterprise unstructured data agents combining file search and web search), and hundreds of thousands of developers since March 2025 launch. The Responses API has processed trillions of tokens across use cases including market research, education, software development, and financial analysis. Available to enterprise customers via Azure OpenAI Service.
adoption_and_market.community_size: OpenAI Developer Community forum has hundreds of thousands of active members. OpenAI Python SDK (openai-python) has ~25,000+ GitHub stars. OpenAI Cookbook has ~60,000+ stars with File Search examples. No separate community specifically for File Search — it is part of the broader OpenAI developer ecosystem.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: OpenAI has raised approximately $57.9B+ in total funding over 9 rounds from 63 investors. March 2025: $40B SoftBank-led Series F at $300B valuation. October 2025: $500B valuation. February 2026: Talks for $100B round at $730-830B valuation with Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, SoftBank participation. IPO potentially targeting H2 2026/2027 at up to $1T valuation.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Direct competitors for managed RAG: Google Vertex AI RAG Engine (tighter GCP integration), Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases (AWS ecosystem), Cohere RAG with Command R+ (multilingual strength), Perplexity Sonar API (web search focused). For file search specifically: competing with self-built RAG using LangChain/LlamaIndex + vector databases (Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant). Key differentiator: zero-infrastructure setup, single API call, built-in with OpenAI's models. Key weakness: vendor lock-in, no model portability, higher cost at scale, limited customization.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Ideal for: (1) Early-stage startups (1-5 engineers) needing RAG capabilities without infrastructure overhead — go from zero to production RAG in hours, not weeks. (2) Non-technical founders using Custom GPTs with file upload for no-code RAG prototypes. (3) Teams already on the OpenAI API wanting to add document Q&A or web-grounded responses. (4) MVPs and POCs where speed-to-market matters more than cost optimization. Less suitable for: startups needing multi-model flexibility, cost-sensitive high-volume applications, or advanced RAG patterns (graph RAG, custom reranking, multimodal embedding). Budget guidance: viable for teams spending <$1K/month on RAG; consider self-hosted alternatives above $5K/month.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Buy (use OpenAI File Search) when: team is small, time-to-market is critical, document volume is modest (<10GB), and you are already committed to the OpenAI ecosystem. Build your own RAG when: you need model portability (e.g., switching to Claude or Mistral), require advanced customization (custom chunking, graph RAG, multimodal), have high query volumes (>100K/month), or need sub-second latency. Hybrid approach: use File Search for prototyping and initial launch, then migrate to self-hosted (pgvector, Pinecone, Qdrant + LangChain/LlamaIndex) as you scale and understand your retrieval needs better.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: Extremely fast. Basic File Search RAG: 1-2 hours to first working prototype (upload files, create vector store, make API call). Production-ready with error handling and UI: 1-3 days. Web Search integration: similar timeline. This is the fastest path to production RAG available today. Comparison: custom RAG pipeline with self-hosted vector DB typically takes 1-4 weeks to production.
key_lessons: 1. Start with managed RAG (File Search) to validate your use case before investing in custom infrastructure — the speed-to-learning advantage outweighs the per-query cost for early-stage products.

2. Be aware of vendor lock-in: File Search only works with OpenAI models. Design your application with an abstraction layer so you can swap retrieval backends later without rewriting your entire application.
3. Monitor costs carefully: vector storage ($0.10/GB/day) and search queries ($2.50/1K) can surprise you at scale. A 50GB knowledge base costs $150/month in storage alone, plus query costs.

4. File Search latency (7-60 seconds) may not meet real-time UX expectations. Test with realistic data volumes early and have a fallback plan (streaming responses, loading indicators) for user-facing applications.

5. Web Search is powerful for grounding but adds significant cost ($25-50/1K calls + context tokens). Use it selectively for queries that genuinely need real-time information rather than as a default for all queries.
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: Yes, partially. ChatGPT Custom GPTs provide a no-code interface for uploading files and enabling knowledge retrieval (File Search). The OpenAI Playground also allows testing File Search and Web Search without code. However, production API integration requires coding. No visual RAG pipeline builder — for that, see alternatives like Dify, Flowise, or LangFlow.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 2 (Prompt Engineering & No-Code Tools — Custom GPTs with File Search), Session 3 (AI Project Framing — Build vs Buy RAG decisions, CRISP-DM application to RAG projects), Session 4 (Business Models — cost analysis of managed vs self-hosted RAG at different scales)

confidence.data_quality: High — based on official OpenAI documentation, OpenAI developer blog posts, OpenAI API reference, pricing pages, and corroborated by developer community discussions and third-party analyses.
confidence.cross_reference: OpenAI official docs (platform.openai.com), OpenAI Developer Community forum, OpenAI Cookbook, VentureBeat coverage, TechCrunch funding reports, eesel.ai practical guide, LlamaIndex benchmark comparison, Medium technical analyses, Microsoft Azure OpenAI documentation.
confidence.caveats: File Search internals (embedding model, index algorithm, reranking model) are not publicly documented — details are inferred or [uncertain]. Pricing is subject to change and varies by model/tool version. Latency reports vary significantly across users and workloads. The Assistants API (which originally hosted File Search) is being deprecated August 2026 in favor of Responses API — migration required. Web Search quality has received mixed reviews with reports of stale results. OpenAI's rapid iteration pace means features and pricing may change frequently.
confidence.security_posture: OpenAI maintains SOC 2 Type 2 compliance (audited January-June 2025), ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701 certifications. Data encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+). API data is not used for model training by default (opt-in only). Data residency options available in 10+ regions for enterprise customers. GDPR and CCPA compliance supported with Data Processing Addendum. Potential concerns: data uploaded to vector stores is processed by OpenAI infrastructure (no self-hosted option), knowledge base poisoning risk if untrusted documents are uploaded, and no disclosed embedding inversion protections specific to File Search.
